answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens and form peer audit graphs verified via topological cut verifications. A cluster cannot fake quorum across an audit ledge: multi-agent cross-examiners decrypt audit trails encrypted by each agent's cipher. Colluding subgraphs entangling like an illicit vine are isolated; when cut bounds fail, stake slashing imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling quadratically with cluster size.
